label: Aquinas, I q.14 a.6 co. and ad 1: God knows creatures in their own natures through his essence
locator: I q.14 a.6 co. and ad 1
interpretation: Aquinas distinguishes proper knowledge of what differentiates creatures from knowledge of being in common. His explanation relies on the divine essence containing creaturely perfections, including differentiating perfections, in a higher manner. The first reply distinguishes the mode of the knower from the nature of the known thing.
attribution: The passage states that through his own essence God knows creatures in their own natures and in what distinguishes them from one another, which is the premise.
